subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Germ cell tumours: histology, staging, serum markers, risk stratification and cisplatin-based curative chemotherapy

steps.tx: Testicular germ cell tumours are broadly classified into seminoma and nonseminomatous germ cell tumours **NSGCT**. Despite marked histopathological diversity encompassing embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumour, choriocarcinoma, and teratoma, all invasive germ cell tumours share a pathognomonic cytogenetic signature: gain of the short arm of chromosome 12, characteristically manifesting as **isochromosome 12p** or 12p amplification.

rows: Normal AFP; mild beta-hCG elevation in < 15%

steps.tx: Accurate clinical staging mandates measuring three serum tumour markers: **alpha-fetoprotein**, **beta-hCG**, and lactate dehydrogenase LDH. Alpha-fetoprotein is synthesized by yolk sac and embryonal elements; crucially, alpha-fetoprotein is never produced by pure seminoma, meaning any elevation in AFP confirms a nonseminomatous component. Serum markers must be reassessed after inguinal orchiectomy to establish post-operative marker decline.

left.title: Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP)
points: Serum half-life: 5 to 7 days
Produced by yolk sac and embryonal carcinoma
Never elevated in pure seminoma
Any elevation mandates treatment as nonseminoma

right.title: Beta-hCG
points: Serum half-life: 24 to 36 hours
Secreted by syncytiotrophoblastic cells
Elevated in choriocarcinoma, embryonal, and seminoma
Rapid decline confirms surgical clearance

steps.tx: The international **IGCCCG classification** system provides structured risk groupings for **metastatic GCT** into good, intermediate, and poor prognostic categories. Risk stratification incorporates histological subtype, primary anatomical site, presence of non-pulmonary visceral metastases, and post-orchiectomy serum tumour marker nadirs. Notably, seminoma patients are categorized only into good or intermediate prognosis, as poor-risk seminoma does not exist.

rows: Testis/retroperitoneal primary; no non-pulmonary visceral mets; S1
Testis/retroperitoneal primary; no non-pulmonary visceral mets; S2
Mediastinal primary, or non-pulmonary visceral mets, or S3 markers

steps.tx: First-line curative chemotherapy for good-risk metastatic germ cell tumours comprises 3 cycles of **BEP** bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin administered every 21 days, or 4 cycles of **EP** etoposide and cisplatin. In clinical trials, 3 cycles of BEP achieved equivalent curative efficacy to 4 cycles while sparing patients from additional cumulative myelosuppressive and pulmonary toxicities, curing over 90% of good-risk individuals.

steps.tx: Patients presenting with intermediate- or poor-risk metastatic disease require 4 cycles of **BEP chemotherapy**. Because cumulative bleomycin exposure elevates the risk of life-threatening pulmonary fibrosis, protocols mandate monitoring cumulative dose below 300 units, serial physical examinations, and baseline pulmonary function testing. Furthermore, patients receiving bleomycin must avoid high fractions of inspired oxygen during subsequent surgical anaesthesia.

left.title: Bleomycin Pulmonary Toxicity
points: Presents with dry cough, dyspnoea, and subcrepitant rales
Basilar interstitial pneumonitis on chest HRCT
Risk escalates above cumulative dose of 300 units
Requires immediate bleomycin discontinuation and steroids

right.title: Anaesthesia Oxygen Restriction
points: High FiO2 generates toxic free radical lung injury
Post-chemotherapy ARDS triggered by hyperoxia
Maintain lowest tolerable FiO2 during general surgery
Avoid excessive intraoperative crystalloid fluid loading

steps.tx: Following completion of chemotherapy for nonseminomatous germ cell tumours, residual retroperitoneal masses measuring **1 cm or larger** on restaging CT mandate nerve-sparing **retroperitoneal lymph node dissection** RPLND. Histopathological examination of resected masses reveals necrotic tissue in 40% to 50%, mature teratoma in 35% to 40%, and viable active germ cell malignancy in 10% to 15% of cases.

steps.tx: Clinical stage I seminoma following radical inguinal orchiectomy achieves cure rates approaching 99%. Because relapse risk is low, guidelines recommend **active surveillance** alone as the preferred management strategy. For patients unwilling or unable to pursue rigorous surveillance, adjuvant options comprise single-cycle **carboplatin** at area under the curve AUC 7 or adjuvant para-aortic strip external beam radiotherapy delivering 20 Gy in 10 fractions.

rows: Preferred; 100% cure with salvage BEP; avoids overtreatment
Single outpatient dose; low acute toxicity; long-term data limited
Para-aortic field; small risk of secondary pelvic malignancies

steps.tx: **Salvage chemotherapy** for relapsed germ cell tumours utilizes conventional-dose TIP combining **paclitaxel**, **ifosfamide**, and **cisplatin**. Alternatively, high-dose chemotherapy using carboplatin and etoposide followed by **autologous stem cell rescue** delivers curative outcomes in approximately 50% of relapsed patients, particularly in patients exhibiting intermediate- or high-risk relapse features.

left.title: Conventional Salvage (TIP)
points: Paclitaxel, Ifosfamide, Cisplatin x 4 cycles
Mesna uroprotection mandatory with ifosfamide
Curative in good-risk first relapse
Avoids intensive myeloablative stem cell transplant

right.title: High-Dose Chemotherapy (HDCT)
points: High-dose Carboplatin + Etoposide x 2-3 cycles
Autologous stem cell infusion after each cycle
Preferred in poor-risk relapse or subsequent salvage
Cures up to 50% of previously refractory patients
